summary.text: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is an undersea mountain ridge along the Atlantic floor that marks a boundary where tectonic plates pull apart.
A deep rift valley runs along its length, where magma from the mantle erupts as lava and makes new crust for the plates.
Mapping in the 1950s showed it is part of a 40,000 km ridge system, a find that led to the theory of seafloor spreading and plate tectonics.

facts.label: Spreading rate
facts.value: About 2.5 cm per year on average

facts.label: Above the sea
facts.value: Rises above sea level in Iceland

facts.label: Formed
facts.value: In the Triassic, on the supercontinent Pangaea

facts.label: Divided by
facts.value: The Romanche Trench, near the equator

items.prompt: A traveler in Iceland walks across the Mid-Atlantic Ridge on dry land. How is that possible?

options.label: The ridge was lifted out of the sea by a meteor
Iceland drifted onto the ridge from Europe
Parts of the ridge stand high enough to clear the sea
The sea around Iceland drained away long ago

items.explain: The ridge is mostly underwater, but some portions are high enough to rise above sea level, as in Iceland.

items.prompt: The plates on either side of the ridge spread about 2.5 cm a year. Roughly how much farther apart do they get over 40 years?

options.label: About 10 cm
About 1 m
About 10 m
About 100 m

items.explain: At about 2.5 cm a year, 40 years adds up to roughly 100 cm, or about 1 m.

items.prompt: In 1872 scientists aboard HMS Challenger came across a large rise in the middle of the Atlantic. What job were they doing?

options.label: Hunting for sunken treasure ships
Tracking schools of migrating whales
Testing an early submarine design
Scouting a route for a telegraph cable

items.explain: The team was investigating a future location for a transatlantic telegraph cable when they found the rise.

items.prompt: Geologists sample rock from the rift valley at the ridge's center and find it is freshly formed lava. Why there?

options.label: Magma from the mantle erupts there to make new crust
Old crust is pushed down and melted there
Ocean currents carry lava there from distant volcanoes
Earthquakes grind old rock into new lava there

items.explain: The rift marks the actual plate boundary, where magma reaches the seafloor, erupts as lava and produces new crust.

items.prompt: What big idea gained acceptance after scientists found that ridges like this one circle the globe?

options.label: That the Earth is slowly shrinking
That oceans are older than continents
That continents drift on moving plates
That the seafloor never changes

items.explain: Finding the worldwide ridge system led to the theory of seafloor spreading and to general acceptance of continental drift in the form of plate tectonics.

items.prompt: When the ridge first formed, rifts opened in three arms, and usually one arm failed. What did many of those failed arms later become?

options.label: Deep ocean trenches
Large river valleys
Tall mountain ranges
Chains of active volcanoes

items.explain: The failed arms, called aulacogens, became many large river valleys in the Americas and Africa, including those of the Mississippi, Amazon and Niger.
